Same ownership-token argument as the accepted rgblevels:params entry, and basicadj is a copy of that code.  Exclusive ownership of g->params passes through the call_auto_exposure state machine, and every handover is under gui_lock even though the payload accesses are not: the pipe writes params only after taking 1 -> -1 at basicadj.c:1419-1423 (process) and :1301-1305 (process_cl), publishes 2 at :1433-1435 / :1334-1336, and _develop_ui_pipe_finished_callback reads params only after taking 2 -> -1 at :279-285.  Only one preview pipe runs at a time -- dt_pipe_is_preview() matches DT_DEV_PIXELPIPE_PREVIEW only, not the distinct PREVIEW2 bit (pixelpipe.h:44,48) -- so two pipe writers cannot overlap, and the two GTK entry points cannot interleave with each other.  The unlocked GTK token write in button_released (:384) can lose a request or a result -- that is the separate box_cood/call_auto_exposure defect, #22120 -- but it cannot produce a concurrent params writer.  Re-check if the token protocol changes or a second pipe gains this path.

_update_histogram() runs on the pipe but never calls GTK: it takes an atomic g_object_ref() on the widget at colorharmonizer.c:305 and hands it to gdk_threads_add_idle() at :306, so the GTK calls happen on the main thread, in _auto_detect_button_enable_idle() at :1332-1348.  The field itself is written only in gui_init() (:1415), so the pipe-side read is of an immutable pointer.  What makes this safe rather than merely tidy is the ref, because nothing cancels the source: gui_cleanup() (:1663-1672) has no g_idle_remove_by_data() drain and the module implements no change_image(), and the source is keyed on the widget rather than on self, so a drain on self could not find it either.  The idle body touches nothing but the ref'd widget before g_object_unref(), and the ref keeps the GObject alive past the gtk_widget_destroy() in dt_iop_gui_cleanup_module(), where set_sensitive/set_tooltip_text on a destroyed-but-not-finalized widget are legal.  The image-switch shape is harmless too: histogram_valid is set FALSE only in gui_init (:1552) and TRUE at :300, so after the first run was_invalid is FALSE and no further source is queued, and a source left over from the old image only re-enables an already-sensitive button.  The unlocked read of g->histogram_valid at :297, outside the private histogram_lock that guards the write at :300, is a separate defect and is filed as #22059.  Re-check if the idle callback starts reaching the module through self, or if histogram_valid gains a reset that can re-arm the queueing path.

Both sites are three lines apart inside _update_histogram -- the unlocked read at :297 and the write under g->histogram_lock at :300 -- and that function is reached only from process():476 and process_cl():679, behind the guard at :266, 'if(!self->gui_data || !dt_pipe_is_preview(piece->pipe)) return;'.  The first clause excludes export, thumbnail, snapshot and duplicate-develop contexts, which have no gui_data; the second excludes preview2 and the full pipe inside darkroom.  What is left is the single preview pipe with a single worker thread, so the two sites cannot race, and no GTK code reads the flag at all -- the button enablement reaches the main thread via gdk_threads_add_idle at :306.  Two things this does not cover, neither of which is this finding: gui_init writes the flag at :1552 before initialising the mutex at :1553, and _update_histogram overwrites the whole histogram with memcpy at :299, which under OpenCL fast tiling would describe only the last strip.  Re-check if a GTK-side reader of histogram_valid appears, or if the :266 guard is relaxed.

The sites are in the GtkDrawingArea handlers (area_draw:2593, area_button_press, area_button_release, area_motion_notify, area_leave_notify), in gui_post_expose:2271, and in static helpers reached only from those: _init_drawing (callers gui_post_expose:2271 and area_draw:2606), init_nodes_x:2565 / init_nodes_y:2579 (sole caller area_draw:2707,:2711, which wraps them in the critical section at :2706/:2710 and whose in-source comment says they must be called holding gui_lock -- the scan reports them unlocked only because lock depth is lexical per function), update_histogram:1473 (callers auto_adjust_exposure_boost:1822, auto_adjust_contrast_boost:1884, area_draw:2618) and invalidate_luminance_cache:624 (callers gui_update:1729, gui_changed:1746, the auto_adjust quads and gui_focus).  Two defects sit on the same code and are not this finding: gui_post_expose:2271 passes self->widget to _init_drawing where area_draw:2606 passes the drawing area, so graph_width, graph_height and inset derive from the wrong allocation until the next area redraw; and max_histogram is only ever raised (compute_log_histogram_and_stats:1469), while toneeq_process:1042,:1130 clears histogram_valid from the pipe without resetting it the way invalidate_luminance_cache:631 does, leaving the inset histogram drawn too short after an upstream change.  Re-check if any of these fields gains a pipe-side access.
